question: Should the Tlon authentication path intentionally cap legacy response-drain compatibility at 64 KiB and 250 ms after real Urbit proof confirms normal cookie acquisition?
rationale: The code trades a previously unbounded compatibility behavior for a fixed cutoff; tests establish mechanics but cannot determine whether the chosen envelope preserves supported Urbit deployments.

options.title: Validate and merge
options.body: Accept the bounded drain after a redacted real Tlon/Urbit login on the final head shows cookie acquisition within the proposed limits.

options.title: Widen or redesign the compatibility envelope
options.body: Adjust the limit or use a server-compatible completion signal if real deployments require longer or larger successful responses.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep the existing behavior until an owner can define and prove the required compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Validate and merge
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded drain after a redacted real Tlon/Urbit login on the final head shows cookie acquisition within the proposed limits.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the proposed implementation and are best placed to supply the missing real-environment evidence; historical area ownership was not established.
